headline: Markets sold off broadly as US-Iran military exchanges escalate and Australia's stronger-than-expected GDP data raises the spectre of an RBA rate hike this month.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS had a rough session today, falling 5.3% to $5.19. Lithium stocks remain under pressure as global lithium prices stay depressed — there's no single catalyst today, but weak sentiment across the sector continues to drag the stock lower. The long-term thesis depends on EV demand picking up; nothing has changed structurally today.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI dropped 3.8% today on the ASX, tracking weakness in US tech and AI stocks from last night. Broader risk-off sentiment (investors pulling back from growth stocks) weighed on the fund. The underlying AI growth story remains intact — this is short-term noise given the sector pullback.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO slipped 1.4% last night in a weak session for the NASDAQ. The pullback comes despite good news — GTA 6 pre-orders have crossed 4.5 million following a Netflix showcase, and Rockstar has confirmed the game world (Leonida) is so vast even their own developers haven't seen all of it. The dip looks like broad market drag rather than any company-specific issue.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft fell 1.2% last night, caught up in a general tech selloff on the NASDAQ. The long-term story remains strong — one analyst note circulating this week suggests MSFT could reach $1,000 by 2031 if AI growth continues as expected. No bad news specific to Microsoft; just a soft market night.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Google dipped 1% last night as tech broadly sold off. Interestingly, Google is reportedly days away from launching Gemini 3.8 Flash (codename Skimaki), a new AI model that could outperform OpenAI and Anthropic in coding tasks. That's a potential positive catalyst coming very soon.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG slipped 0.9% today, reflecting the broad ASX pullback. As a diversified fund holding Australian and global equities, it's naturally moved with the market. Nothing to be concerned about — this is what a diversified fund does in a soft session.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS eased 0.6% today on the ASX, mirroring last night's soft US session. Still sitting in profit overall (+1.76% on your total investment). A minor pullback in a down market — no action needed.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE was the quiet achiever today, essentially flat (+0.05%). Emerging markets held steady while developed markets sold off — a small sign of resilience. Still marginally in the red overall but nothing concerning.

watch_today.title: Pilbara Minerals (PLS): Sitting on a 23% loss — hold steady
watch_today.detail: PLS dropped another 5.3% today to $5.19, and you're now down 23% on your investment. That stings, but the lithium sector as a whole is in a downcycle waiting for EV demand to accelerate. There's no structural collapse in the company — Pilbara is one of the world's top lithium producers. Selling here locks in the loss; long-term holders sit tight and wait for the cycle to turn.

watch_today.title: GXAI: AI ETF down 14.5% overall — but the theme is about to heat up
watch_today.detail: GXAI fell 3.8% today and is down 14.5% on your total investment. However, with Google about to launch a new Gemini model that could leapfrog OpenAI and Anthropic in coding (expected this week), and both Anthropic and OpenAI also releasing new models, the AI sector is very active right now. If anything, this dip could be a chance to top up — but only if you're comfortable with the volatility. Hold for now, watch the Google Gemini launch closely.

watch_today.title: RBA rate hike risk is real — GDP surprise changes the picture
watch_today.detail: Australia's economy grew faster than expected in the latest GDP print, and AFR is now saying the RBA has the data it needs to lift interest rates this month. A rate hike (i.e. the Reserve Bank raising the cost of borrowing) would likely pressure growth stocks and property. Keep an eye on the RBA meeting — this is the biggest near-term risk to your portfolio's Aussie holdings.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA 6 hype building — hold and watch
watch_today.detail: Take-Two fell 1.4% last night but the underlying news is positive: GTA 6 pre-orders have hit 4.5 million after a Netflix showcase event, and Rockstar is generating massive buzz. You're still down 6.7% overall on TTWO, but the GTA 6 release remains the big catalyst ahead. Long-term hold — don't let a quiet market night shake you out of this one.

watch_today.title: Google Gemini model launch expected this week — watch GOOG and GXAI
watch_today.detail: Reports say Google is days away from releasing Gemini 3.8 Flash (Skimaki), a model targeting top performance in coding tasks — potentially beating both OpenAI and Anthropic. If the launch lands well, this could be a near-term positive catalyst for both GOOG and GXAI. GOOG is already up 8% on your total investment. No action needed, but keep an eye on the announcement.

watch_today.title: US-Iran military conflict escalating — broad market risk
watch_today.detail: The US and Iran exchanged military strikes overnight in the biggest flare-up since July. Trump has vowed further retaliation. Oil is already elevated at $89/barrel, and markets sold off broadly. If this escalates further, expect more volatility across your US holdings and global ETFs. Not a reason to sell anything, but worth watching closely this week.

world.summary: The biggest story today is a serious military escalation between the US and Iran. Meanwhile, Canada-US trade tensions are simmering, Russia is secretly arming Iran, and Trump's administration continues to target political opponents.

stories.title: US and Iran trade military strikes in biggest exchange since July
stories.why_it_matters: The US military struck Iranian targets overnight, and Tehran fired back at US bases — the most significant exchange of fire between the two countries since July. President Trump has publicly vowed more strikes in retaliation for Iran's response. Oil prices are sitting at $89/barrel and markets sold off broadly on the news. This is a genuine geopolitical flashpoint: if it escalates further, expect oil to spike, markets to get nervy, and your US-heavy portfolio to feel it. For everyday Australians, higher oil prices mean higher petrol prices.

stories.title: Russia secretly helping Iran develop supersonic cruise missiles
stories.why_it_matters: A new report reveals Russia has been secretly helping Iran develop supersonic cruise missiles — weapons that are much harder to intercept than conventional missiles. This comes as the US-Iran conflict heats up, making Iran potentially more dangerous as a military adversary. It also deepens the Russia-Iran alliance and raises the stakes in any US military confrontation. For global markets, it adds another layer of uncertainty to an already tense situation.

stories.title: Canada's PM Carney tells Trump officials to 'stop throwing shade' over trade talks
stories.why_it_matters: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has publicly pushed back at Trump administration officials, telling them to stop making snide comments ('throwing shade') while Canada-US trade negotiations are still ongoing. The US-Canada trade relationship is one of the world's largest, and ongoing tension keeps uncertainty high for businesses on both sides of the border. For Australian investors with US exposure, prolonged trade disputes add noise to an already volatile environment.

stories.title: Trump administration targeting individuals including former FBI chief James Comey
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration has published a list of individuals it is targeting, including former FBI Director James Comey. Separately, a whistleblower has raised concerns that the US Postal Service is rushing to comply with a Trump executive order in a 'sloppy' way. These stories point to an ongoing pattern of the administration using federal power against political opponents and institutions — something legal groups like Protect Democracy are actively challenging in court. It's a reminder that US political risk remains elevated heading toward the next election cycle.

stories.title: US pushes light-touch approach to AI regulation at G20 tech meeting
stories.why_it_matters: At the G20 tech ministers meeting, the US is pushing for a 'hands-off' approach to regulating AI — basically arguing governments should let the industry develop without too many rules. The EU is going the other way, pushing for stricter laws. Elon Musk also weighed in at the G20, defending AI data centres and attacking EU regulations. For investors in AI stocks (like GOOG, MSFT, GXAI), lighter US regulation is generally a positive — it means fewer compliance costs and faster product rollout for American tech companies.

markets.summary: A broad selloff last night in the US and today on the ASX, driven by escalating US-Iran military conflict and nerves about global growth. Tech was hit hardest on the NASDAQ. Gold pushed higher as investors sought safety, while oil dipped slightly despite the Middle East tension — suggesting markets still think the conflict might be contained. The Aussie dollar edged lower.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: The ASX closed down nearly 1% today, dragged by the global risk-off mood and domestic concerns about a potential RBA rate hike after stronger-than-expected GDP data.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: The S&P 500 fell 0.7% last night, weighed down by geopolitical tension (US-Iran) and a weak tech sector.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: The NASDAQ dropped over 1% last night — tech stocks bore the brunt of the selloff, with Google, Microsoft and most AI-related names falling.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil actually fell slightly despite the US-Iran conflict — markets seem to be pricing in a limited, contained exchange rather than a full-blown war. Watch this closely if tensions escalate.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold rose 0.7% as investors moved toward safe-haven assets amid geopolitical stress. Gold at $4,379/oz is a reminder of how uncertain the global outlook feels right now.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar slipped slightly to 71.5 US cents. A weaker AUD is mildly positive for your US holdings when converted back to Australian dollars.

politics.summary: The big domestic story today is Australia's economy growing faster than expected — which sounds like good news, but it's raising real fears that the RBA (Reserve Bank of Australia) will hike interest rates this month. The RBA is also making moves to reduce its reliance on US dollar reserves.

stories.title: Australian economy grows faster than expected — RBA rate hike now on the table
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's latest GDP (economic growth) figures came in stronger than expected, meaning the economy is running hotter than the Reserve Bank would like. AFR is now reporting the RBA has the data it needs to justify lifting interest rates at its September meeting. Higher interest rates mean more expensive mortgages and loans — a real cost-of-living hit for Aussie households. It also tends to put downward pressure on share prices, especially growth stocks. For the ASX, this is a headwind heading into next week.

stories.title: RBA cuts US dollar reserves as central banks hedge against Trump
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank of Australia has been quietly reducing its holdings of US dollars as part of its foreign currency reserves. The move reflects a broader trend among central banks globally — hedging against uncertainty created by Trump's economic and trade policies. It's a sign that even Australia's own central bank is less comfortable relying on the US dollar as a stable anchor than it once was. Doesn't directly affect your portfolio, but it's an interesting signal about where confidence in US economic leadership sits right now.

ai.summary: The AI model race is moving fast — Google is days away from releasing a new Gemini model that could challenge OpenAI and Anthropic in coding, while regulators in the US and EU are heading in opposite directions on how tightly to govern AI. Good news overall for your GOOG and GXAI holdings.

stories.title: Google about to launch Gemini 3.8 Flash — could beat OpenAI and Anthropic in coding
stories.why_it_matters: Google is expected to release its new Gemini 3.8 Flash model (internally codenamed 'Skimaki') as early as this week. Reports suggest it's been internally tested against OpenAI and Anthropic models, and could take the top spot in coding performance benchmarks — a highly competitive and commercially valuable area of AI. This matters for GOOG holders: a strong model launch would reinforce Google's position in the AI race and is a positive signal for the stock. It's also good for GXAI, which holds AI-linked companies.

stories.title: Anthropic and OpenAI also launching new models
stories.why_it_matters: Google isn't alone in racing to market — Anthropic (maker of Claude) and OpenAI (maker of ChatGPT) are also launching new models this week. The AI model competition is intensifying, with all three major players releasing upgrades at the same time. For investors, this is a sign the sector is innovating rapidly, which is good for the long-term theme, even if it means no single company dominates permanently.

stories.title: US pushes light regulation for AI at G20; EU goes the opposite way
stories.why_it_matters: At the G20 tech ministers meeting, the US argued for minimal government interference in AI development — essentially, let companies build freely. The EU is pushing for stricter rules and legal accountability. This regulatory divergence creates a split environment: US AI companies (like Google and Microsoft) benefit from fewer rules at home, while operating under tougher requirements in Europe. For long-term AI investors, lighter US regulation is a tailwind for American tech companies' profitability.

stories.title: Banks and big tech square off over 'agentic AI' regulation in Australia
stories.why_it_matters: 'Agentic AI' refers to AI systems that can take independent actions — like booking appointments, executing trades, or managing tasks without a human approving every step. In Australia, big banks and big tech companies are clashing over who should be responsible when these systems make mistakes. Banks want strict rules; tech firms want flexibility. This is an emerging regulatory debate that will shape how AI gets deployed in Australian financial services — worth watching as the technology matures.

sport.summary: NRL Round 27 is coming up with plenty to watch — the premiership race is heating up and there's significant controversy over a delayed rule-change communication. The Sydney Swans scandal also took a major turn today.

stories.title: NRL premiership race heating up heading into Round 27
stories.why_it_matters: With Round 27 underway, NRL.com reports the cream is rising to the top of the ladder as the finals race enters its final stretch. The Titans host the Dolphins at Cbus Super Stadium on the Gold Coast on Friday at 6pm — a local match worth watching. The Broncos face the Bulldogs on Thursday night to kick things off.

stories.title: Bulldogs coach Ciraldo slams NRL over rushed rule-change communication
stories.why_it_matters: Canterbury Bulldogs coach Cameron Ciraldo has publicly called out the NRL for giving clubs inadequate notice of a rule change, saying teams haven't had time to properly prepare. While the specific rule wasn't detailed in the headline, coaches publicly criticising the governing body is unusual and suggests frustration is building at the top end of the competition.

stories.title: Sydney Swans scandal: Police narrow focus to four players, not looking for anyone else
stories.why_it_matters: Police investigating the Sydney Swans alleged sexual assault scandal have confirmed they are 'not looking for anyone further' and have narrowed their focus to four specific players. A suspended Swans star has also broken cover publicly for the first time since the hotel incident emerged. The investigation is clearly narrowing — this saga is heading toward a resolution that will have significant consequences for the players involved and the club.

stories.title: Perth NRL expansion: Sua signs with the new team in a 'massive opportunity'
stories.why_it_matters: The new Perth NRL franchise is starting to take shape, with player Sua signing up and calling it a 'massive opportunity.' The expansion into Perth is a major development for the game's growth in Western Australia and will add a new dynamic to the competition when the team enters the NRL. Player signings will be closely watched over coming months as the roster takes shape.
